question: Whether the already acquired statewide NM source can close an actual Senate candidate-menu native integration gap, and whether a source-to-native draft advances owner work.

current_owner_state.finding: NM remains among the nine held settings (26/35 supported); v35 still reports no new menu settings closed and points to the earlier proposal/root review. No later owner admission or successor selection was found in the cited current artifacts.

selection.relevant_selection: NC_NM retains printed-person identities/corroboration, while qualified-write-in support remains unclosed.

existing_menu_proposal.finding: The two proposed NM IDs are sourced to the older Santa Fe County master list; proposal status is support_unclosed, conditional and pending root selection. It predates the statewide portal packet.

prior_root_review.finding: Its browser-failed portal and county-only scope describe an earlier state; its held-write-in and cutoff conclusions remain relevant.

statewide_source.scope: SOS-homepage-linked 2026 General Election Candidate List; County filter 99 labeled State, all contests and all parties selected; unpaged one-page response with 524 rows.
statewide_source.write_in_observation: Six rows in other contests explicitly carry a '(write-in)' suffix; none of the four US Senate rows does. This is evidence of statewide coverage and portal display capability, not proof there are no unrecorded, later, or legally qualifying Senate write-ins.
statewide_source.retrieval_and_cutoff: Retrieved October 25, 2026. Neither portal nor saved source metadata establishes exact publication/status availability by the October 20 forecast cutoff; do not backdate this evidence.

draft_mapping.eligible_named_menu_role: printed candidate, conditionally supported at Oct 25 retrieval
printed candidate, conditionally supported at Oct 25 retrieval

exclude_from_menu.treatment: Retain as source evidence/status; do not materialize as a candidate option.
Retain as source evidence/status; do not materialize as a candidate option.

implementation_notes: A source-to-native draft is worthwhile: bind the existing two source-local IDs to the statewide portal rows, preserve exact literal party codes and status/date fields, and keep the older county list and ballot as corroboration rather than primary statewide scope.
Do not add candidate axes or globally merge identities. Translate party code to model affiliation only in a separately explicit mapping; leave caucus assignment null.

Keep the finite menu conditional and support_unclosed; list only the two observed qualified printed names. Do not encode the lack of a Senate write-in row as an empty legal write-in set or an authenticated none certificate.

remaining_blockers: Root/source owner selection and admission are absent; this review is not an admission or native input change.
October 25 retrieval cannot support the October 20 forecast information set. Any use requires a later dated input/forecast or independent as-of publication evidence; it cannot be backdated.

Portal roster/status does not independently establish qualified write-in closure, legal write-in markability/validity, or election-day immunity from revisions. Preserve the existing write-in hold until a supported complete statewide certificate/roster or explicit no-certificate conclusion appropriate under the operative rule is selected.

A complete native model-side problem still requires owner bindings for candidate utility roles, incumbency, caucus behavior, and source-specific participation/choice; party labels alone do not set caucus.
recommendation: Prepare a narrow source-to-native successor draft in the owner workflow if the owner wants to advance NM's conditional named printed menu. It materially improves the source scope from county ALL ballotstyles/precincts to the statewide State-selected all-party/all-contest portal and distinguishes Qualified from Disqualified Senate rows. It does not close NM support, legal write-in domain, Oct 20 cutoff, fit, or public qualification.
